facts.fact: A new part-of-speech tagger is presented.
facts.supporting_span: We present a new part-of-speech tagger

facts.fact: The part-of-speech tagger demonstrates explicit use of both preceding and following tag contexts.
facts.supporting_span: (i) explicit use of both preceding and following tag contexts

facts.fact: The part-of-speech tagger uses a dependency network representation.
The part-of-speech tagger makes broad use of lexical features.
The part-of-speech tagger jointly conditions on multiple consecutive words.
facts.supporting_span: including jointly conditioning on multiple consecutive words

facts.fact: The part-of-speech tagger makes effective use of priors in conditional loglinear models.
facts.supporting_span: (iii) effective use of priors in conditional loglinear models

facts.fact: The part-of-speech tagger models unknown word features in a fine-grained way.
facts.supporting_span: (iv) fine-grained modeling of unknown word features

facts.fact: The resulting tagger gives a 97.24 % accuracy.
facts.supporting_span: the resulting tagger gives a 97.24 % accuracy

facts.fact: The 97.24 % accuracy is on the Penn Treebank WSJ.
The tagger achieves an error reduction of 4.4 %.
The error reduction is measured on the best previous single automatically learned tagging result.
facts.supporting_span: on the best previous single automatically learned tagging result
